name: dsads
paper_title: Recognizing daily and sports activities in two open source machine learning environments using body-worn sensor units
notes: 19 activities x 8 subjects x 60 five-second segments = 9,120 files, 5 Xsens MTx units (torso, right arm, left arm, right leg, left leg) x 9 channels (acc/gyro/mag xyz) at 25 Hz. VERIFIED AT CONVERT TIME: median |acc| 9.731 m/s^2 (gravity present), |gyro| p99.9 max 21.06 rad/s. SEGMENT RE-JOIN, VERIFIED NOT ASSUMED: a 5 s segment cannot fill a 6 s analysis window, so the converter re-joins s01..s60 into the original 5-minute recording. UCI states the division is temporal; the converter CHECKS it by comparing the sample step across each join with the steps inside the segments. Measured over all 8,968 joins: median ratio 1.09 (an unrelated segment pair scores ~5x), so the ordering is temporal — but 8.1% of joins are genuine discontinuities, and the converter SPLITS the session at those rather than smoothing them, so no window straddles a gap. PLACEMENT CORRECTION (2026-08-09): UCI names the five column blocks T, RA, LA, RL, LL, which reads as torso/arms/legs. The paper is more precise and the converter follows it -- 'two of the +/-18g sensor units are placed on the sides of the knees (the right-hand side of the right knee and the left-hand side of the left knee), the remaining +/-18g unit is placed on the subject's chest, and the two +/-5g units on the wrists'. So the placements are chest, right wrist, left wrist, right knee, left knee. This matters because HALO conditions on the placement text: calling a wrist sensor 'the right arm' would mis-describe the only two watch-like placements this dataset has. The paper also confirms 25 Hz, 8 subjects (4F/4M, ages 20-30), 5-minute recordings divided into 5-second segments.
